britannica-1911-pereyaslavl:
Pereyaslavl, a town of Russia in the government of Poltava, is described in the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica. It stands where the Trubezh and Alta rivers meet, south-east of Kiev. Five miles lower down, its port village sits on the Dnieper. The town and its three suburbs held 14,609 people.

Vladimir the Great founded Pereyaslavl in 993, marking a great win over the Pechenegs. From 1054 it headed a separate principality of its own. As a southern outpost it figures often in the wars of three centuries. The Mongols plundered it in 1239, yet it rose again. Later it became a centre of the Cossack movement. By the Treaty of Pereyaslavl in 1654, the Cossack chief Bogdan acknowledged the rule of the Russian tsar. Its trade, the article notes, ran in grain, salt, cattle, and horses.
